```{r}
##Let's import the species-level information
abundance_table_species <- read.delim("~/Downloads/abundance_table_species.tsv")

##Let's split column 'tax' into true taxonomy columns
# Split the 'tax' column into multiple new columns
abundance_table_species.2 <- abundance_table_species %>%
  separate(col = tax,
           into = c("Domain", "Kingdom", "Phylum", "Class", "Order", "Family", "Genus", "Species"),
           sep = ";",
           remove = TRUE, # Set to FALSE if you want to keep the original 'tax' column
           extra = "merge", # Ensures that if there are more than 8 splits, they are merged into the 'Species' column
           fill = "right")

##We can now use this to create taxonomy and count files
###First, taxonomy###
taxonomy_df <- abundance_table_species.2 %>% 
  select(Domain, Kingdom, Phylum, Class, Order, Family, Genus, Species)

##We will need row names to create the phyloseq object. Since we do not have ASVs/OTUs but unique species, we will use species as rownames
row.names(taxonomy_df) <- taxonomy_df$Species

###Now, let's create the count file###
count_df <- abundance_table_species.2

##set row names
row.names(count_df) <- count_df$Species

##Remove the first eight taxonomy columns including the 'Species' column to clean up the dataframe
count_df <- count_df %>%
  select(-Domain, -Kingdom, -Phylum, -Class, -Order, -Family, -Genus, -Species)

##Replace 'X5080' with 'Sample' in the column names
colnames(count_df) <- gsub("X5080_", "Sample_", colnames(count_df))

##Now for sample data
sample_df <- read.csv("~/Documents/DeQueen_Litter/sample_df.csv")

##Modify the sample_df dataframe
names(sample_df)[names(sample_df) == "Treat"] <- "Treatment"

##Add 'Sample_' prefix to every row in 'Sample.ID'
sample_df$Sample.ID <- paste("Sample_", sample_df$Sample.ID, sep = "")

##Replace values in 'Treatment' column
sample_df$Treatment <- ifelse(sample_df$Treatment == "LT", "IndigoLT", sample_df$Treatment)
sample_df$Treatment <- ifelse(sample_df$Treatment == "CON", "Control", sample_df$Treatment)

##Remove Sample 15 (did not sequence), change Sample 15-2 to Sample 15 (to match taxonomy and count files), and remove blank rows
# Remove rows where 'Sample.ID' is 'Sample_15' or 'Sample_'
sample_df <- sample_df[!(sample_df$Sample.ID %in% c("Sample_15", "Sample_")), ]

# Rename 'Sample_15-2' to 'Sample_15'
sample_df$Sample.ID <- ifelse(sample_df$Sample.ID == "Sample_15-2", "Sample_15", sample_df$Sample.ID)

##Set row names based on the 'Sample.ID' column
rownames(sample_df) <- sample_df$Sample.ID

# Add the 'bio_or_control' column based on conditions in 'Treatment'
sample_df <- sample_df %>%
  mutate(bio_or_control = ifelse(Treatment %in% c("IndigoLT", "Control"), "biological", "control"))

```

```{r}
##We can now create the phyloseq object
# Convert sample_df to a sample_data object
sample_data_ps <- sample_data(sample_df)

# Convert count_df to an OTU table (make sure counts are integers)
otu_table_ps <- otu_table(as.matrix(count_df), taxa_are_rows = TRUE)

# Convert taxonomy_df to a tax_table object
taxonomy_table_ps <- tax_table(as.matrix(taxonomy_df))

# Combine into a phyloseq object
physeq <- phyloseq(otu_table_ps, sample_data_ps, taxonomy_table_ps)

```

```{r}
##Let's decontaminate with the decontam package
##https://link.springer.com/article/10.1186/s40168-018-0605-2
##Based on code from soybean manuscript

#library(decontam)

##Assign negative control
sample_data(physeq)$is.neg <- sample_data(physeq)$bio_or_control == "control"

##Create a presence-absence phyloseq object
physeq.pa <- transform_sample_counts(physeq, function(abund) 1*(abund>0))
physeq.pa.neg <- prune_samples(sample_data(physeq.pa)$bio_or_control == "control", physeq.pa)
physeq.pa.pos <- prune_samples(sample_data(physeq.pa)$bio_or_control == "biological", physeq.pa)

##Perform decontamination with different prevalence thresholds

##Threshold 0.1
contamdf.prev01 <- isContaminant(physeq, method="prevalence", neg="is.neg", threshold=0.1)

# Create data.frame of prevalence in positive and negative samples
df.pa01 <- data.frame(pa.pos=taxa_sums(physeq.pa.pos), pa.neg=taxa_sums(physeq.pa.neg),
                      contaminant=contamdf.prev01$contaminant)

# Plot the results for threshold 0.1
ggplot(data=df.pa01, aes(x=pa.neg, y=pa.pos, color=contaminant)) + 
  geom_jitter(size=2.5, alpha = 0.75) +
  xlab("Prevalence (Negative Controls)") + 
  ylab("Prevalence (True Samples)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size=16),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        legend.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)) +  
  scale_color_manual(name = "Contaminant", labels = c("False", "True"), values = c("#2f357c","#bf3729")) +
  ggtitle("Prevalence threshold = 0.1")

#ggsave("Decontam_prevalence_threshold_0.1.png", width = 10, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 900)

##Threshold 0.5
contamdf.prev05 <- isContaminant(physeq, method="prevalence", neg="is.neg", threshold=0.5)

# Create data.frame of prevalence in positive and negative samples
df.pa05 <- data.frame(pa.pos=taxa_sums(physeq.pa.pos), pa.neg=taxa_sums(physeq.pa.neg),
                      contaminant=contamdf.prev05$contaminant)

# Plot the results for threshold 0.5
ggplot(data=df.pa05, aes(x=pa.neg, y=pa.pos, color=contaminant)) + 
  geom_jitter(size=2.5, alpha = 0.75) +
  xlab("Prevalence (Negative Controls)") + 
  ylab("Prevalence (True Samples)") +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(axis.text = element_text(size=16),
        axis.title = element_text(size = 16),
        legend.title = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10),
        legend.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 10)) +  
  scale_color_manual(name = "Contaminant", labels = c("False", "True"), values = c("#2f357c","#bf3729")) +
  ggtitle("Prevalence threshold = 0.5")

#ggsave("Decontam_prevalence_threshold_0.5.png", width = 10, height = 10, units = "in", dpi = 900)

# Write out the results for final analysis
#write.csv(df.pa05, "./DecontamResults_prev05.csv")

# Remove contaminants identified with a threshold of 0.5
physeq_decontam <- prune_taxa(!contamdf.prev05$contaminant, physeq)

```

```{r}
##We will now prune the negative controls and get busy with analyses
##Remove negative controls from the physeq_decontam object
physeq_decontam_no_neg <- prune_samples(sample_data(physeq_decontam)$bio_or_control == "biological", physeq_decontam)

##Convert Growout and House to character in the sample data
# Extract sample data as a dataframe
sample_data_df <- as(sample_data(physeq_decontam_no_neg), "data.frame")

# Check the class of sample_data_df to confirm it is a dataframe
print(class(sample_data_df))

# Convert Growout and House to character
sample_data_df <- sample_data_df %>%
  mutate(Growout = as.character(Growout),
         House = as.character(House))

# Convert the dataframe back to sample_data object
sample_data(physeq_decontam_no_neg) <- sample_data(sample_data_df)

```
